The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{3}{5},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $tan⁡\theta .$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/fc291f1fc5c4a712d3eef7ea2872de621855669d97445b24a2bc7a9da55949d9.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{3}{5}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{3}{5}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{3}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{9}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{4}{5}.$

Finally, knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{3}{5})}{(\frac{4}{5})}=\frac{3}{4}.
$$
